why the outcome happened.

defs_parts: Five labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a made-up run with a fixed seed, so it comes out the same every time.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: A fluent, accurate explanation can still mislead about the world.
SHAP reports the model's internal accounting and stays on Rung one.
A Shapley value is a marginal contribution averaged over every order of arrival.
Efficiency makes the values add up, and no axiom promises correctness.
LIME can change between runs, and a counterfactual is the model's answer.
Explainable is not interpretable, so ask who is reading the report.
bookends.segment: Model Or World, Name The Term
bookends.command: Give me short cases about explaining a model's prediction, one at a time. For each case I must name the exact term, chosen from fluency trap, shortcut, internal accounting, marginal contribution, Shapley value, Efficiency, LIME instability, counterfactual, interpretability and language-game mismatch, and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then correct me in two sentences.
checks: Check: each case needed one exact term, and the answer waited for you.
Check: every correction said why the look-alike term did not fit.
